controls.label: x_1 (first input location)
controls.help: Slides the first point along the horizontal axis; changes predicted value y-hat_1, residual r_1, squared residual r_1^2 and SSE.

controls.label: x_2 (second input location)
controls.help: Slides the second point along the horizontal axis; changes predicted value y-hat_2, residual r_2, squared residual r_2^2 and SSE.

controls.label: y_1 (first observed label)
controls.help: Raises or lowers the first observed value; changes residual r_1, squared residual r_1^2 and SSE, leaving y-hat_1 fixed.

controls.label: y_2 (second observed label)
controls.help: Raises or lowers the second observed value; changes residual r_2, squared residual r_2^2 and SSE, leaving y-hat_2 fixed.

controls.label: intercept b0
controls.help: Moves both predicted values by the same amount; changes y-hat_1, y-hat_2, r_1, r_2, both squared residuals and SSE.

controls.label: slope b1
controls.help: Tilts the candidate line; changes y-hat_1 and y-hat_2 by different amounts, hence r_1, r_2, the squared residuals and SSE.

explorations.title: Flat line at zero intercept
explorations.instruction: Predict: when the slope is zero and the intercept is zero, what are the two residuals and how large is SSE? Then apply the preset, which sets x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2, intercept and slope.
explorations.observe: Both predicted values become 0, the residuals become 2 and -2, the squared residuals become 4 and 4, and the SSE readout becomes 8.
explorations.why: A zero slope removes the b1 x term, so each predicted value equals the intercept 0; the residuals are then just the observed labels, and SSE adds 4 + 4.

explorations.title: Line passing through both observed points
explorations.instruction: Predict: can both residuals be zero at the same time? Then apply the preset, which sets x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2, intercept and slope.
explorations.observe: Predicted values become 1 and 2, matching the observed labels, so residuals are 0 and 0, squared residuals are 0 and 0, and the SSE readout becomes 0.
explorations.why: Intercept 1 and slope 1 reproduce both observed labels, so y_i minus y-hat_i is 0 at each point; squaring keeps zero and the sum of the two squares stays zero.
